actions.action: Check whether the pot has drainage holes
Buy a pot 1-2 inches wider with drainage holes
Buy potting soil and perlite/pumice/bark and mix 30-40% amendment
Repot: slide plant out, loosen outer roots, set at same height or slightly lower, fill with fresh mix
Trim any black, mushy or dead roots
Water thoroughly after repotting and let drain
Alternative: top-dress with a layer of fresh soil as a stopgap
Place in bright indirect light with some morning sun
Check top 1-2 inches of soil and water when dry, letting excess drain
If many leaves yellow and drop, check watering and light
Feed diluted balanced fertilizer every 2-4 weeks in spring/summer
Prune leggy branches for fuller shape

reason: The answer notes depleted 2-year-old soil and recommends repotting with regular soil, matching the fix, but frames the plant as having 'not much' wrong and never mentions rootbinding; the top-dress stopgap is flagged as insufficient, so it is not harmful.
